faq: Is a PWA as good as a native app?
For many apps, such as portals, trackers and booking tools, yes. For heavy graphics, deep device features or background tasks, a native app is better. We tell you honestly which one fits your idea.
Can it go in the app stores?

A PWA is installed from the browser. Google Play can list packaged web apps and we can discuss that route, but store approval is theirs and Apple has stricter rules, so we do not promise a store listing.
Do push notifications work on iPhone?
On recent iPhones they work once the app is added to the home screen, with limits set by Apple. We build to those rules and test on a real device before handover.
Can you turn my website into one?
Often yes. If your site is a clean web app, adding install, offline pages and a manifest is quick. If it is an older site, we review it first and tell you what needs fixing.

desc:
Progressive web app development gives you one app that installs from the browser, opens full screen and keeps working on a weak connection. Ecom Swift LLC builds your PWA for iPhone, Android and desktop from a single codebase, with no store listing required.

## What is a progressive web app?

A progressive web app, or PWA, is a website built with extra abilities that make it feel like an installed app. It has an icon on the home screen, opens without browser bars and can show useful pages even when the network drops. It is delivered through a web address, so users never have to visit an app store to get it.

Behind this sits a web app manifest, which describes the name, icon and colors, and a service worker, which is a small script that caches pages and handles offline behavior. Together they make a normal site installable and resilient.

## Why build a PWA instead of two native apps?

Native iPhone and Android apps are built separately, reviewed separately and updated separately. For many businesses that is more cost and more waiting than the idea deserves. A PWA is written once, runs everywhere a modern browser runs and updates the moment you publish a change, with no review queue.

It also removes a big hurdle for users. People tap a link and start using the app straight away, instead of searching a store, downloading it and signing up before they see any value. The trade-off is that some deep device features are limited, especially on iPhone, so we check your must-have features early.

## How a PWA affects your results

Speed and convenience drive usage. A page that opens instantly from the home screen gets used more often than a bookmark buried in a browser. Offline pages mean field staff, delivery drivers or travelers can still view their lists without a signal, and entries made offline are saved and sent later.

Push notifications, where the device and browser support them, bring people back with a useful reminder. The effect on sign-ups, repeat use or time saved depends on your audience and how useful the app is, but removing friction at the first visit is a reliable place to start.

## What a great PWA includes

- A valid manifest with name, icons, theme color and a start page.
- A service worker with a sensible caching plan for pages, images and data.
- Offline fallback pages that explain what is available without a connection.
- A splash screen and app theme so it feels like a product, not a bookmark.
- Responsive layouts tested on a phone, a tablet and a desktop browser.
- Quick loading, with images sized correctly and scripts kept lean.
- Secure delivery over HTTPS, which installable apps require.
- Optional login, saved data and background sync for returning users.
- Push notifications where the platform supports them, with a clear opt-in step.

## What we do

We confirm what the app must do, then design the screens and the offline behavior together. We build the app, add the manifest and service worker, and test installation on real iPhone and Android devices as well as desktop browsers.

The Basic package covers a small installable app with offline pages. Standard adds more screens, data saved offline and synced later, push notifications where supported, a theme and user login. Premium adds offline sync with conflict handling, a camera or location feature, a link to payments or subscriptions, a Lighthouse speed report and a handover call. Add-ons include extra screens, Play Store packaging and an offline sync upgrade.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Decide which tasks truly need to work offline.
- Keep the first screen light so the app opens instantly.
- Ask for notification permission only after the user has seen the value.
- Try the install flow on an actual iPhone and an actual Android handset.
- Plan how offline changes should merge when the connection returns.

**Avoid:**
- Caching everything, which can leave users looking at stale information.
- Promising features that a specific device does not allow.
- Asking for location or camera access before it is needed.
- Treating install as automatic, since users still need a clear prompt.
- Copying a heavy desktop site into the app without trimming it.

## Who it is for

A PWA suits a business that wants an app presence without two separate builds, a field team that needs forms and lists in places with poor signal, and an existing website owner who wants returning visitors to have a home screen shortcut. It also suits a startup testing an idea before paying for native development.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of what the app should do, your logo and brand colors, and any existing website or API it should connect to. Tell us which devices your users have. We never ask for passwords. If we need to deploy to your hosting, you grant access as a collaborator or developer user.
